headline: Anthropic is shopping a draft AI safety bill to Congress
body: Politico reported that Anthropic has been shopping a draft AI safety bill to Congress, and a spokesperson confirmed the draft. In it, the Commerce Department would have to ask a D.C. judge to halt a model's release after evaluators flag an imminent catastrophic risk.
note: The draft would expressly forbid any federal agency from halting a model's distribution on its own. For a bank that depends on frontier models, the open question is how a court step would affect release timing.

evidence.text: Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s a request for comment but a spokesperson did confirm the draft bill to Politico.
In Anthropic’s draft bill, when evaluators determine that an imminent catastrophic risk is posed, they would have 72 hours to contact the Commerce Department about it.
The Commerce Department would then have to request to a D.C. judge to halt the model’s release.
The legislation would expressly forbid any federal agency from having the discretion to halt the model’s distribution on its own, Politico writes.
